concepts.title: Organising Raw Data into Frequency Distributions
concepts.definition: Raw numbers become readable once they are sorted and tallied: an ungrouped distribution pairs each distinct value with its frequency, while a grouped distribution packs values into class intervals. The frequencies must account for every observation, and the display can be a bar graph, histogram, frequency polygon or ogive.
concepts.key_idea: Sort first, tally second, and check the tally adds up to the number of observations.

solution_steps.action: arrange the observations from smallest to largest
solution_steps.explain: order exposes repeats and prepares medians and quartiles

solution_steps.action: tally each value or class and write its frequency
solution_steps.explain: the frequency counts occurrences, and for grouped data classes must not overlap

solution_steps.action: add the frequency column and match it to the number of observations
solution_steps.explain: a mismatch means an observation was skipped or double counted

concepts.title: Class Mark of a Class Interval
concepts.definition: A grouped distribution speaks through one representative number per class, its class mark: the midpoint sitting exactly halfway between the lower and upper class limits.
concepts.key_idea: Average the two class limits; the midpoint stands for every observation in the class.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_010_descriptive_statistics.txt, section 10.2, grouped data in class intervals with class marks

solution_steps.action: average the two class limits
solution_steps.explain: the midpoint lies equidistant from both ends of the interval

concepts.title: Arithmetic Mean of Ungrouped Data
concepts.definition: The ordinary average splits the grand total of the observations evenly: add every value, then divide by how many values there are.
concepts.key_idea: Sum everything, divide by the number of observations.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_010_descriptive_statistics.txt, section 10.3, mean of ungrouped data as sum of values over their count

solution_steps.action: share the grand total over the observations
solution_steps.explain: the mean is the even share per value

concepts.title: Mean of Grouped Data by Frequency Method
concepts.definition: Grouped observations no longer appear individually, so each class mark is weighted by its frequency: multiply every class mark by its frequency, add the products, and divide by the total frequency.
concepts.key_idea: Weight each midpoint by how often it occurs, then divide by the total weight.

solution_steps.action: weight one class mark by its frequency
solution_steps.explain: f times x is the row contribution of that class

solution_steps.action: divide the summed products by the summed frequencies
solution_steps.explain: fx_sum is the total of the fi xi column and f_sum the total of the f column

concepts.title: Median of Ordered Data
concepts.definition: The median is the value sitting in the middle once the data are sorted: the single central value for an odd count, and the average of the two central values for an even count. Outliers drag the mean but leave the median standing.
concepts.key_idea: Sort, land on position (n + 1) over 2, and average the two neighbours when the count is even.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_010_descriptive_statistics.txt, section 10.3, middle value of the ordered data, average of the two middle values when even

solution_steps.action: find the middle position in the ordered list
solution_steps.explain: position (n + 1) over 2 points at the median slot

solution_steps.action: average the two central ordered values
solution_steps.explain: a and b are the two middle values, identical when n is odd

concepts.title: Mode as the Most Frequent Value
concepts.definition: The mode is the value carrying the largest frequency. A distribution may show one mode, several modes, or no mode at all when no value repeats, which is why the frequency column, not arithmetic, decides it.
concepts.key_idea: Pick the value with the tallest tally; ties and zero repeats are legal outcomes.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_010_descriptive_statistics.txt, section 10.3, the mode is the most frequent value, one mode, several, or none

solution_steps.action: name the value with the highest frequency as the mode claim
solution_steps.explain: check for ties, which give several modes, and for all-ones columns, which give none

concepts.title: Mean Deviation about the Mean
concepts.definition: Mean deviation averages how far the observations sit from the mean, ignoring direction: take each absolute gap, weight grouped gaps by frequency, and average over the total frequency.
concepts.key_idea: Absolute gaps only; direction is thrown away before averaging.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_010_descriptive_statistics.txt, section 10.4, MD as sum of fi times absolute difference divided by total frequency

solution_steps.action: measure one observation's undirected distance from the mean
solution_steps.explain: the absolute value removes the sign of the gap

solution_steps.action: weight the gap by the row frequency
solution_steps.explain: grouped data repeats a gap f times

solution_steps.action: average the weighted gaps over all observations
solution_steps.explain: wg_sum totals the weighted column and f_sum the frequencies

concepts.title: Variance as Mean Squared Deviation
concepts.definition: Variance measures spread by averaging the squared distances of the observations from their mean, so misses far from centre are punished much harder than misses near it.
concepts.key_idea: Square every deviation, then average the squares.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_010_descriptive_statistics.txt, section 10.4, variance as sum of squared deviations of xi from the mean divided by n
question_patterns: find the variance of 2, 4, 6, 8 whose mean is 5

solution_steps.action: take one observation's signed distance from the mean
solution_steps.explain: deviations are measured from the centre

solution_steps.action: square the deviation
solution_steps.explain: squaring makes every contribution positive and stresses big misses

solution_steps.action: average the squared deviations
solution_steps.explain: sq_sum totals the squared column over count observations

concepts.title: Standard Deviation in Data Units
concepts.definition: The standard deviation is the positive square root of the variance; undoing the square returns the spread to the same unit the data were measured in.
concepts.key_idea: Take the positive square root of the variance to get back to original units.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_010_descriptive_statistics.txt, section 10.4, standard deviation is the positive square root of variance and returns to the data unit
question_patterns: find the standard deviation of data whose variance is 9

solution_steps.action: average the squared deviations from the mean
solution_steps.explain: sq_sum over count rebuilds the variance first

solution_steps.action: take the positive square root
solution_steps.explain: the root restores the original measuring unit

concepts.title: Quartiles and Their Positions
concepts.definition: Quartiles slice sorted data into four equal parts: the lower quartile Q1, the median Q2, and the upper quartile Q3. For n ordered observations the cutting positions follow from n plus 1 divided by 4 and three times that.
concepts.key_idea: Q2 is just the median; Q1 and Q3 sit a quarter and three quarters of the way along the ordered list.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_010_descriptive_statistics.txt, section 10.5, quartiles split ordered data into four parts, Q1, Q2, Q3

concepts.title: Interquartile Range
concepts.definition: The interquartile range is the width of the middle half of the data: the upper quartile minus the lower quartile, blind to whatever extremes sit outside.
concepts.key_idea: Spread of the central 50 percent; extremes are ignored by construction.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_010_descriptive_statistics.txt, section 10.5, the interquartile range is Q3 minus Q1 and measures the spread of the middle half

solution_steps.action: subtract the lower quartile from the upper quartile
solution_steps.explain: the gap between the quarter marks is the middle-half spread

concepts.title: Coefficient of Variation
concepts.definition: The coefficient of variation expresses the standard deviation as a percentage of the mean, letting data sets with different units or wildly different averages be compared for relative consistency; the smaller coefficient belongs to the steadier set.
concepts.key_idea: Relative spread, not absolute spread; lower percentage wins the consistency contest.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_010_descriptive_statistics.txt, section 10.5, CV as standard deviation over mean times 100, lower CV means more consistent

solution_steps.action: scale the standard deviation by the mean
solution_steps.explain: the ratio strips the units and the size effect

solution_steps.action: quote the ratio as a percentage
solution_steps.explain: multiplying by 100 gives the coefficient of variation
